headline: Kompany hospitalized; Saka facing weeks out for Arsenal
paragraphs: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital on Friday after collapsing at the club's training ground, a story carried independently by Sky, BBC and the Guardian. The Guardian, citing the club, says Kompany had been nursing a virus and is undergoing further examination; BBC and Sky report the same core facts without extra detail. None of the three say anything yet about his condition or how long he might be away from the touchline.

Arsenal's Bukayo Saka is facing an extended spell out after leaving Friday's 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich with a quadriceps injury. BBC Sport reports he could be out for up to eight weeks; the Guardian, quoting manager Mikel Arteta, frames it as a possible six-week absence. Arteta himself told reporters it's 'difficult to understand the extent' of the issue, so treat both figures as estimates rather than a settled timeline, during a stretch in which Arsenal are trying to defend their title.

Elsewhere among the six: PSG's Ligue 1 match against Lyon was pushed back 24 hours, per the BBC, with planned protests in Paris cited as the reason. Real Madrid feature only in Clasico preview pieces from the Guardian and Opta Analyst ahead of Saturday's trip to Barcelona, with nothing beyond preview analysis reported. At Liverpool, Sky Sports says Florian Wirtz has shown 'signs of life' in recent games while manager Andoni Iraola wants more from him, and FourFourTwo separately reports Dominik Szoboszlai limped off with a hamstring injury against Brentford.
